# Scenario

A committee member at your half-time control has objected that the binary LSAS outcome hides the difference between moderate and severe symptoms.
Another member replies that “more categories always means more nuance.”
You have been asked to prepare a multinomial analysis to address these comments.

# Your task

Use the STePS data to model the three post-treatment LSAS severity categories:

- low/no-to-mild: `< 50`;
- moderate/marked: `>= 50` and `< 80`; and
- severe/very severe: `>= 80`.

Your Quarto notebook must include:

1. the category definitions;
2. the participant-by-category long transformation required by `mlogit`;
3. a check that every participant has three alternatives and exactly one observed choice;
4. a multinomial treatment model;
5. treatment-specific category probabilities with 95% CIs;
6. between-group differences for each category; and
7. a discussion of the sample size within each treatment-by-severity subgroup.
